title: Preferred growth scenario for urban boundary expansion
subtitle: Short-term rental report referred, Elora hockey alcohol pilot, audited financials, Park Road rezoning, tourism washroom without Moloks.
overview: Council endorsed Scenario 3 as the preferred way to estimate how much land the Fergus and Elora-Salem urban centres need for growth to 2051 {{vote:m5}}. Staff will use it when they bring back revised urban boundaries. Delegates for landowners and for agriculture argued in opposite directions, and councillors weighed farmland protection against realistic housing targets.

Council also received the draft short-term rentals report, directed that it be posted on Connect CW and referred it to the Economic Prosperity & Growth Advisory Committee before any by-law is drafted {{vote:m7}}. It approved the 2023 audited financial statements and an Asset Retirement Obligations policy {{vote:m4}}, and approved a pilot allowing alcohol service in part of the tiered seating at Elora Rocks games {{vote:m10}}.

Other decisions: rezoning 22 Park Road from industrial to highway commercial {{vote:m8}}, a parking agreement for Salem Public School {{vote:m11}}, a $5,000 top-up for public engagement in the Housing Needs Assessment {{vote:m12}}, and building the tourism washroom without Moloks {{vote:m14}}. No report came out of the closed session.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed Scenario 3 as the preferred scenario for land need for settlement boundary expansion in Fergus and Elora-Salem and directed staff to use it for revised boundaries.
Council received the draft consultant report, directed staff to post it to Connect CW for feedback and referred it to the Economic Prosperity & Growth Advisory Committee.

decisions.item: 2023 audited financial statements and ARO policy
decisions.detail: Council approved the audited consolidated financial statements presented by KPMG and authorized a by-law approving the Asset Retirement Obligations policy.
Council approved the Official Plan Amendment and zoning change from industrial to highway commercial, with the plan amendment sent to the County for approval.

Council approved a 2024/2025 pilot allowing alcohol service in a section of the tiered seating, evaluated game by game, with authority to discontinue or adjust it delegated to the Managing Director of Community Services.
Council directed staff to build the tourism washroom as originally designed without Moloks and to work with the BIAs and County Solid Waste on downtown garbage.
Council endorsed an in-year budget top-up of $5,000 to add public engagement to the Housing Needs Assessment.
Council authorized a parking agreement with the Upper Grand District School Board for part of the Robert Street unopened road allowance.

debate: A consultant for a landowner argued the higher density and intensification targets are unrealistic and that the Township should rely on the original County analysis. Staff and the Township's consultant said Scenario 3 is realistic and achievable, pointing to densities already seen in the South Fergus secondary plan.

A delegate for the Federation of Agriculture supported Scenario 4 because it preserves the most farmland. Staff and the consultant said Scenario 4 would need much higher intensification and density, and that these were unlikely. A local developer delegate asked for land to be included in the urban boundary.

Councillors raised concerns about farmland quality, daycare and other services, and whether higher buildings could be considered in some locations to protect farmland. Staff said these would be addressed through later work such as zoning reform, phasing and servicing.

On short-term rentals, delegates described noise, parking and absentee-owner problems and asked for stronger enforcement. Councillors worried about costs to the Township and short review time, which led to the referral to the advisory committee.

On alcohol at Elora Rocks games, councillors asked about responsibility if something goes wrong, over-service, accessible exits and cleanup. Staff pointed to the safe service plan, security staff and the municipal alcohol policy.
